status: Public baseline: built from public regulation, replaced by the bank's own questionnaire when received
sources: CBUAE Operational Risk Management Regulation, Circular C 1/2026 (crosswalk IE-REP-003)
UAE Information Assurance Regulation (control families via grc-workbench control library)
UAE Personal Data Protection Law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021
note: CBUAE obligations sit on the bank. These questions cover what the bank needs from its supplier to meet them.

text: Every Critical control Met (answered Yes and management will sign for it)
No High control answered No or Not sure

questions.title: Valid trade licence covering services
questions.question: Is your trade licence valid, and does it cover every service you would sell to the bank?
questions.why: The bank must assess you as a provider before contracting; an expired licence or an activity not on it ends the conversation.
fix: Check the licence expiry date and the listed activities against your service list.
If an activity is missing, apply to your free zone or DED to add it before quoting.
Put the renewal date on a renewal register with reminders at 60, 30 and 7 days.
Keep a current copy ready to send with any tender response.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up

questions.title: Filings, tax and renewals up to date
questions.question: Are all statutory filings, tax registrations and renewals up to date, with nothing overdue?
questions.why: Banks check public registers and tax status; anything overdue is read as weak control.
fix: List every legal date: licence, visas, establishment card, audit, Corporate Tax, VAT.
Clear anything overdue first, including penalties.
Give one accountant responsibility for statutory filings.
Review the list every month.
questions.ie_service: Business Security Audit: renewal register set-up

questions.title: Named security owner
questions.question: Is one named person accountable for information security, with the time and authority to act?
questions.why: Banks want a named security contact who can answer for controls and incidents.
fix: Name the person in writing, with a deputy.
Record their responsibilities in the security policy.
Give the bank their name and contact details at onboarding.

questions.title: Approved information security policy
questions.question: Do you have a written information security policy, approved by management and reviewed at least once a year?
questions.why: The bank's own ICT and cyber policy must extend to its providers; it will ask for yours.
fix: Adopt a short policy set: acceptable use, access and MFA, devices, data handling, incidents, backup, suppliers.
Have management approve and date it.
Brief every person who works on client accounts.
Diary the annual review.

questions.title: PI and cyber insurance
questions.question: Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and have you decided on cyber insurance, at levels a bank would accept?
questions.why: Banks require proof of cover before contract and check a provider's financial standing.
fix: Ask the bank or tender for its minimum limits.
Get two quotes from a broker for PI and cyber cover.
Bind cover before the contract starts and keep the certificate ready to send.
Put the renewal date on the renewal register.

questions.title: Financial statements available
questions.question: Could you show the bank your latest financial statements if asked?
questions.why: The bank must monitor the financial condition of providers it relies on.
fix: Prepare the latest annual accounts, audited if your licence requires it.
Agree with your accountant what can be shared and under NDA.
Keep a one-page financial summary ready for tenders.

questions.title: Bank and CBUAE audit rights in contract
questions.question: Would your standard contract accept the bank's audit and inspection rights, including examination by CBUAE?
questions.why: CBUAE requires banks' contracts to give audit access and allow CBUAE examination for critical outsourcing.
fix: Read your terms for audit, inspection and regulator access clauses.
Add a clause allowing the client, its auditors and its regulator to audit on reasonable notice.
Have the terms legally reviewed.
questions.ie_service: Contract review (GRC advisory with legal partner)

questions.title: Obligations flowed to subcontractors
questions.question: If you use subcontractors or partners, do your contracts with them pass on the same security, confidentiality and audit obligations?
questions.why: CBUAE requires the same protections to flow to subcontractors.
fix: List every subcontractor that could touch bank data or systems.
Add flow-down clauses: confidentiality, security, audit, incident notice, no further subcontracting without approval.
Get each subcontractor to sign.

questions.title: Data processing agreement
questions.question: Do you have a data processing agreement ready for clients whose personal data you handle?
questions.why: UAE PDPL requires processors to act on documented instructions; banks will not share personal data without one.
fix: Adopt a data processing agreement template under the UAE PDPL (and DIFC or ADGM law where relevant).
Reference it in your terms of business.
Keep a record of which clients have signed it.

questions.title: Exit plan: return or delete data
questions.question: Do you have an exit plan: at contract end, return or securely delete the bank's data and hand over the service?
questions.why: CBUAE requires viable exit plans for outsourcing arrangements.
fix: Write a one-page exit plan: what is returned, what is deleted, in what time, and how deletion is confirmed.
Add the exit commitment to your contract.
Test it once with a dummy client folder.

questions.title: Data location known, UAE possible
questions.question: Do you know where any bank data you hold would be stored, and could you keep it in the UAE if required?
questions.why: Banks must keep their master system of record in the UAE, including when outsourced.
fix: List every system that would hold bank data and its storage region.
Choose UAE-region services (for example Microsoft UAE North) or keep no copy outside the bank's environment.
State the data location in your proposal.

questions.title: Confidentiality agreements signed
questions.question: Has everyone who could access client information signed a confidentiality agreement?
questions.why: Banks require confidentiality from everyone with access, including contractors.
fix: Add a confidentiality clause to employment and contractor agreements.
Get existing staff and contractors to sign.
Keep signed copies on file.

questions.title: Background screening
questions.question: Are staff and contractors background-checked at hiring, and can they complete a client's screening if asked?
questions.why: Banks screen people who access their systems and expect suppliers to cooperate.
fix: Define basic checks at hiring: identity, right to work, references.
Agree that staff will complete a client's screening (for example a police clearance certificate) when requested.
Record that the checks were done, not the results.

questions.title: Annual security awareness training
questions.question: Do all staff complete security awareness training at least once a year, with a record of completion?
questions.why: CBUAE expects the bank's risk approach to be communicated to third parties.
fix: Run a short annual course: phishing, passwords and MFA, reporting incidents.
Record names and completion dates.
Repeat for new joiners within their first month.

questions.title: Same-day leaver access removal
questions.question: When someone leaves, is all their access removed on their last day?
questions.why: Leavers with live access are a common cause of incidents.
fix: Keep a list of every account each person has.
Use a leaver checklist; disable accounts on the last day.
Review all accounts every quarter.

questions.title: MFA on all accounts
questions.question: Is multi-factor authentication on for every account that reaches company or client data: email, cloud, remote access and admin?
questions.why: Account takeover is the commonest way into a supplier, and through it into the bank.
fix: List every business account.
Turn on MFA with an authenticator app or key; avoid SMS where possible.
Enforce it centrally (Google Admin or Microsoft Entra Conditional Access).
Record the method per account.

questions.title: Password manager, no shared accounts
questions.question: Are passwords unique and held in a password manager, with no shared accounts?
questions.why: Shared and reused passwords defeat every other access control.
fix: Deploy a business password manager with MFA on it.
Replace shared logins with named accounts.
Move credentials in and change each to a generated password.

questions.title: Encrypted laptops and phones
questions.question: Are all laptops and phones encrypted (BitLocker, FileVault or built-in phone encryption), with recovery keys held safely?
questions.why: A lost unencrypted laptop is a reportable data breach.
fix: Turn on BitLocker or Device Encryption on Windows, FileVault on Mac, a passcode on phones.
Store recovery keys in the password manager or the company admin console, never only on the device.
Confirm with manage-bde -status C: and keep the result.

questions.title: Work devices not shared
questions.question: Are work devices used only by authorised staff, and never shared with family or others?
questions.why: A bank's questionnaire asks whether devices are used only by authorised staff.
fix: Issue work devices to named people only.
Give family members their own device or a separate account.
State the rule in the acceptable use policy.

questions.title: Supported and patched systems
questions.question: Are operating systems and software supported and patched within 14 days (critical fixes faster)?
questions.why: CBUAE requires banks to manage obsolete systems, including those run by third parties.
fix: Turn on automatic updates on every device.
Replace any unsupported operating system or software.
Check update status monthly.

questions.title: Endpoint protection on every device
questions.question: Is anti-malware or endpoint protection running and up to date on every device?
questions.why: Malware on a supplier device can reach bank data and accounts.
fix: Use Microsoft Defender or an equivalent endpoint product on every device.
Manage it centrally so alerts are seen.
Check weekly that every device reports in.

questions.title: SPF, DKIM and enforced DMARC
questions.question: Does your email domain publish SPF, DKIM and an enforced DMARC policy?
questions.why: Without them anyone can send email as you, including fake invoices to the bank.
fix: Enable DKIM signing in your email platform.
Publish DMARC at p=none with reports, then move to quarantine, then reject.
Protect parked domains with a null SPF record and DMARC reject.

questions.title: Independent, tested backups
questions.question: Are backups kept independently and encrypted, with a restore tested at least every quarter?
questions.why: CBUAE requires continuity and recovery capability, including at providers the bank depends on.
fix: Keep a second copy separate from the working device or tenant, encrypted.
Restore one real file each quarter and log the result.
Fix and re-test any failure.

questions.title: Asset inventory
questions.question: Do you keep an up-to-date list of devices, systems and cloud services in use?
questions.why: The bank must know which of its supplier's systems touch its data.
fix: List devices, software and cloud services with owner and end-of-support date.
Update it when anything is added or removed.
Review it quarterly.

questions.title: Limited admin rights, separate accounts
questions.question: Are administrator rights limited to the people who need them, using separate admin accounts?
questions.why: Everyday accounts with admin rights turn one phishing email into full control.
fix: Remove admin rights from everyday accounts.
Create separate admin accounts with MFA for the few who need them.
Review admin membership quarterly.

questions.title: Security alerts logged and reviewed
questions.question: Are sign-in and security alerts logged and reviewed?
questions.why: Detection depends on someone looking at the alerts.
fix: Turn on audit logging in your email and cloud platform.
Set alerts for risky sign-ins and mailbox forwarding rules.
Review alerts weekly, or use a monitored service.

questions.title: Independent vulnerability test
questions.question: Have you had an independent vulnerability scan or penetration test in the last 12 months?
questions.why: CBUAE expects stress and penetration testing, and banks extend this to key providers.
fix: Commission an external vulnerability scan of your internet-facing services.
Fix high and critical findings and re-test.
Keep the summary ready for the bank.

questions.title: Rules for AI tools
questions.question: Do you have rules for AI tools, so no client data goes into public AI services?
questions.why: Bank data pasted into a public AI tool leaves the bank's control.
fix: Write a one-paragraph AI use rule into the acceptable use policy.
List approved business AI tools whose terms exclude training on your data.
Brief staff.

questions.title: Incident response plan
questions.question: Do you have a written incident response plan with named roles and contact details?
questions.why: CBUAE requires banks to run a full incident lifecycle, which depends on providers responding properly.
fix: Write a short plan: report, contain, assess, notify, recover, review.
Name who does what, with phone numbers.
Run a 30-minute tabletop exercise once a year.

questions.title: Incident notice fast enough for CBUAE deadlines
questions.question: Could you notify the bank of an incident affecting it fast enough for the bank to meet CBUAE's 4-hour, 24-hour and 72-hour reporting deadlines?
questions.why: Banks must notify CBUAE within 4 hours of events affecting Critical Operations and within 72 hours of high-risk incidents; they pass this down to suppliers.
fix: Commit in your contract to notify the bank within the time it sets (often 1 to 4 hours of awareness).
Keep a notification template: what happened, which services, actions taken, expected recovery.
Make sure partners notify you fast enough to meet it.

questions.title: Incident log
questions.question: Do you keep a log of security incidents and near misses, reviewed for lessons?
questions.why: No log means no evidence of control.
fix: Start an incident log, even if it is empty: date, what, impact, action, lesson.
Review it monthly.
Feed lessons into policies and training.

questions.title: Tested business continuity plan
questions.question: Do you have a business continuity plan covering loss of systems, premises and key people, tested at least once a year?
questions.why: CBUAE requires continuity for Critical Operations, including scenarios like key staff being unavailable.
fix: Write a short continuity plan: what stops, how you keep serving clients, recovery times.
Name a deputy and set up break-glass access to key accounts.
Test once a year and record the result.

questions.title: Own suppliers assessed
questions.question: Do you assess the security of your own critical suppliers (cloud, software, subcontractors)?
questions.why: The bank's supply chain includes your suppliers.
fix: List your critical suppliers.
Check each one's security terms or certifications.
Review yearly and keep a record.

questions.title: Privacy notice and PDPL compliance
questions.question: Have you published an accurate privacy notice and do you meet your obligations under the UAE PDPL?
questions.why: Banks will not share customer data with a provider that cannot show PDPL compliance.
fix: Publish a privacy notice that matches what you actually do.
Keep a one-page record of what personal data you hold, why, where and for how long.
Name who handles data subject requests.

questions.title: Certification or dated plan
questions.question: Do you hold a security certification (for example ISO/IEC 27001), or have a dated plan to get one?
questions.why: Certification shortens bank due diligence; a plan shows direction.
fix: Decide which certification your buyers ask for.
Run a gap assessment and set a target date.
Share the plan with the bank if not yet certified.

questions.title: Independent review in last 12 months
questions.question: Has your security been independently reviewed in the last 12 months?
questions.why: An independent review is the bank's assurance that your answers are true.
fix: Commission an independent review against a recognised standard.
Fix the findings and keep the summary.
Repeat every year.
